title: Garage Line
subject: a retired bus mechanic in Fresno whose HO-scale model railway grows out of the spare room, across the hallway and through a hole in the garage wall, until his wife's car is parked on the street and she asks for a station named after her
caption: Surf rock revival, early-60s instrumental surf sound played by a 2020s revival band, with vocals. Reverb-drenched Fender guitar with fast tremolo-picked lead lines; a spring-reverb rhythm guitar chopping eighths; a reedy Farfisa organ; round electric bass; driving surf drums with tom fills. Vintage spring-reverb garage room sound, live-band feel. Male baritone, plain and cheerful, light group 'ooh' backing on the chorus. 150 BPM, E minor. Sunny, frantic and proud. No modern pop production, no distortion-heavy punk, no autotune, no synthesizers, no ballad section.
lyrics:
[Intro - tremolo lead guitar and surf drums]

[Verse 1]
Started with a loop on a table top
Little red engine, one small stop
Then the spare room's full of plastic hills
Track on the dresser and the windowsills

[Pre-Chorus]
Drilled a hole through the hallway wall
Train goes by when you take a call

[Chorus]
Garage line, garage line
Running every hour right on time
Through the wall and past the paint
Wife's car out on the street, she's a saint

[Verse 2]
Bridge of balsa over cans of oil
Tiny cows in a box of soil
She stands in the doorway, keys in hand
Asks me where her car is meant to land

[Chorus]
Garage line, garage line
Tunnel where the mower parked, now it's mine
Through the wall and past the paint
Wife's car out on the street, she's a saint

[Bridge - organ and tremolo guitar]
She says build a station, paint it blue
Put my name on it and I'll ride it too

[Outro - surf guitar break, drums fade]
Next stop Linda, ring the bell
Garage line is running well
